before.html:
Question 1
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=2t−9t2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=−2m/s when t=1s, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment t=2s.

a
24m/s
b
16m/s
c
20m/s
d
12m/s
e
4m/s
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=t^2-3t^3+C. Since v(1)=-2, C=0. Thus v(2)=4-24=-20 m/s, so the speed is |v(2)|=20 m/s.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t-9{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t-9{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=-2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =(1)^{2}-3(1)^{3}+C \\ -2 & =1-3+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =(2)^{2}-3(2)^{3} \\  & =4-24 \\  & =-20\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $20\,\text{m/s}.$

after.html:
Question 1
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=2t−9t2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=−2m/s when t=1s, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment t=2s.

a
24m/s
b
16m/s
c
20m/s
d
12m/s
e
4m/s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(2t−9t2)dt=t2−3t3+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=−2. Substituting this into the above gives

−2=(1)2−3(1)3+C−2=1−3+CC=0.

Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=t2−3t3.

We evaluate the velocity at time t=2s:

v(2)=(2)2−3(2)3=4−24=−20m/s

Finally, since the speed is equal to |v(t)|, we conclude that the speed of the particle is 20m/s.

before.html:
Question 2
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=−6e−2t, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=12e−t−10
b
 v(t)=−2e−2t+4
c
v(t)=3e−2t−1
d
 v(t)=3e−2t+2
e
 v(t)=−2e−t+2
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating a(t)=-6e^{-2t} gives v(t)=3e^{-2t}+C. Using v(0)=2 yields 3+C=2, so C=-1. Therefore v(t)=3e^{-2t}-1.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-6{e}^{-2t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-6{e}^{-2t})\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2t})+C \\  & =3{e}^{-2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =3{e}^{0}+C \\ 2 & =3+C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3{e}^{-2t}-1.$

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{6}{{t}^{2}}-3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{6}{{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t+\int (-3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{6}{t}-3t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-\frac{6}{2}-3(2)+C \\ 1 & =-9+C \\ C & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-\frac{6}{t}-3t+10.$
